deepdive.sec: Building Materials / Engineered Wood & Interior Solutions

bull_bear.body: Priority on sweating existing assets for ROCE improvement; Balance sheet discipline (targeting <1x long-term debt/EBITDA); Century Ports treated as separate profit center; No dividend/buyback specific commentary, focus on reinvestment for capacity.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical instability impacting chemical supply chains and forex volatility; Raw material price inflation outpacing pricing power; Execution risk on new greenfield projects; Competition in MDF leading to selective price rollbacks by peers.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on structural demand and brand equity; Cautious on providing specific FY27 guidance due to global fluidity (war/uranium mentions); Disciplined on capital allocation; Bullish long-term on MDF despite near-term noise.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly stated Century Ports provides no direct cost savings to the Ply business but serves as a separate profit center; Old Particle Board technology being completely scrapped rather than repurposed; Outsourcing in Plywood being phased out entirely for quality control despite capacity constraints.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The capex cycle has been debt-funded: Total Debt rose from Rs 239.07 crores (2022-23) to Rs 656.52, Rs 1,383.12, Rs 1,531.26 crores and Rs 1,644.21 crores at Q1 26-27, taking Total Debt/Equity from 0.16 to 0.65.
- Leverage metrics peaked with the build and are now easing: Total Debt/EBITDA went 0.52 (2022-23) to 1.27, 2.97 (2024-25), 2.47 (2025-26) and 2.20 (Q1 26-27); Interest Cover fell from 31.15 to a low of 4.15 in 2025-26 before recovering to 4.93.
- Returns are still far below the pre-capex level: Return on Avg Equity went 24.52% (2022-23) to 10.37% (2024-25), recovering to 13.09% (2025-26) and 13.52% (Q1 26-27); Return on Avg Capital Employed went 30.91% to 12.30%, then 13.43% and 14.39%.
- The debt mix has shifted from import-linked to bank funding: Capex Buyers' Credit fell from Rs 378.71 crores (2024-25) to Rs 232.52 crores (Q1 26-27) while Short Term Debt (From Banks) rose from Rs 538.11 crores to Rs 811.79 crores; there is no debt from related parties and no foreign-currency long-term debt in any year shown.
- Cash is run thin against this debt - Cash, Bank & Liquid Funds fell from Rs 278.21 crores (2022-23) to Rs 49.14 crores (2024-25) and stood at Rs 82.32 crores at Q1 26-27.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Plywood: Rev +17.9% YoY, EBITDA margin 16.1%; Laminates: Rev +16.3% YoY, margin turnaround to 10.3% (from 5.2% FY25); MDF: Rev +31% YoY, margin 11.3% (pressured by chemical costs/ATL spend); Particle Board: Rev +108% YoY, margin 7.2% (ramping new capacity).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The deck is organised around six reported revenue streams, each with its own volume and financial slide: Plywood (with Decoply and Commercial Veneer), Laminates, MDF (Plain and Prelam), Particle Board (Plain and Prelam), Logistics Services and "Others".
- Logistics Services is a genuinely different business inside the group - the deck shows it running at a gross profit of 81.3% of total income in FY2025-26 (vs 32.5% for the consolidated entity), on a much smaller base of Rs 159.07 crores total income.
- Century Ply Standalone is only part of the story: the Summary - Consolidated P&L slide reconciles the standalone entity to consolidated through a long list of subsidiaries - Auro Sundaram; Century Furniture; Ara, Arham, Apnapan, Adonis; Century Infotech; Century Panel; Century MDF; Century Infra; Century Pacific; Century Ports; and Century Gabon - together with their consolidation adjustments and non-controlling interests.
- Capital employed is now heavily panel-led: consolidated Fixed Assets grew from Rs 1,062.69 crores (2022-23) to Rs 2,809.40 crores (Q1 26-27), while shareholder's equity (including share capital of Rs 22.25 crores) went from Rs 1,910.62 crores to Rs 2,713.32 crores.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Myanmar impairment] "Extra-ordinary items in the FY 2022-23 pertains to impairment loss in our Myanmar subsidiary amounting to Rs 49.25 crores" - the write-off sits in the Plywood segment's financials.
- [Labour law / gratuity] "Exceptional items in FY 25-26 pertains to gratuity impact of labour law."
- [Entry tax settlement] "In FY 23-24 Sales and other expenses include Rs 7.13 crores towards settlement of Entry Tax Liability as per Amnesty Scheme of West Bengal Government."
- [Tax regime] "The company has opted for the new tax regime from the financial year 2021-22."
- [Presentation basis] The safe harbor states the figures are "re-grouped/re-casted/re-arranged for facilitating financial analysis and may not confirm to statutory formats" and that "All the figures except for the whole year are unaudited" - so these segment cuts are not the statutory numbers.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Input cost inflation (chemicals/resin) due to geopolitical conflicts; 15% price hike in MDF/Particle Board and 7% in Plywood implemented to cover costs; ATL spend in Q4 impacted MDF margins temporarily; timber prices stable.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Muted 10-12% for Plywood next year due to high base; Margin: Targeting high-teens for MDF steady-state; Order Inflow: Stable demand post-price hikes; Capex: Focused on Hoshiarpur (Ply) and brownfield expansions, no frozen large capex for MDF/PB yet.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not applicable; company operates on make-to-stock/distributor inventory model; management noted April sales remained robust despite March channel stocking.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Plywood capacity to increase 30% in FY27 (Hoshiarpur greenfield + brownfield); MDF brownfield debottlenecking (+60-70k cum) completing Q1FY27; Potential greenfield in UP/Orissa by FY28-29; Century Ports commenced operations (Khidderpore) targeting cash positivity in Q1FY27.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Century Plyboards delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 1,492 cr, +24.5% YoY) and expanded EBITDA margins to 13.6% (ex-forex) driven by operating leverage and a turnaround in Laminates, while initiating strategic capex in Plywood and entering port logistics to secure supply chain advantages despite near-term chemical cost inflation.
